english.title: Do an act to facilitate the commission of a breach of UK immigration law by a non EU person
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) did an act, namely **(..SPECIFY THE ACT..), which facilitated the commission of

(A)_[a breach]_
(B)_[an attempted breach]_

of immigration law, namely **(..SPECIFY THE SECTION AND LEGISLATION ALLEGED TO HAVE BEEN / ATTEMPTED TO HAVE BEEN BREACHED..), in that **(..SPECIFY THE BREACH / ATTEMPT..), by a person, namely **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..), who was not a citizen of the European Union, knowing or having reasonable cause for believing that the act facilitated the commission of

(C)_[a breach]_
(D)_[an attempted breach]_

of immigration law by that person and that the person was not a citizen of the European Union
english.legislation: Contrary to section 25(1) and (6) of the Immigration Act 1971.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location

investigatoraction.description: Criminal lifestyle offence under Schedule 2 to POCA - consider confiscation order

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) As substituted by section 143 of the Nationality, Immigration and Asylum Act 2002 as from 10/02/03.
(ii) Options (B) and (D), 'attempted breach', inserted by paragraph 2 of Schedule 14 to the Immigration Act 2016 on 31 May 2016. These options should not be used in relation to incidents occurring prior to this date.
(iii) For offence committed after 23:00 on 31st December 2021 refer to H22353/IM71131.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Fourteen years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
